hook: Tarnaka's name may come from a *wire* fence or a telegraph office
hook_b: Tarnaka's name may come from a *wire* fence or a telegraph office
tldr: Two local stories explain Tarnaka: a wire-fenced Nawab's mango orchard with a guard at the gate, or a telegraph office where people sent 'taar'.

beats.what: Tarnaka is commonly explained as 'Taar' (wire) plus 'Naka' (checkpost), Siasat reports.
beats.why: One story: a Nawab's mango orchard was fenced with wire and guarded at the entrance. Another: 'taar' also means telegram, and Tarnaka had a telegraph office.
beats.care: A BSNL office still stands at the junction; local accounts say the area had vineyards in the Nizam's time, with grapes reportedly grown until the 1980s.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Before flyovers and the metro station, Tarnaka was farmland, according to local Instagram accounts cited by Siasat.
